deportes.t: We have not found any strength training trial in hikers. Going downhill puts a lot of load on the knee, and in the Alps three out of four falls happened on the way down: strong legs for braking could help, but it is a deduction.
p: In 12 healthy people, walking downhill loaded the knee with 8 times body weight, compared with 3.9 on the flat; 80% of it came from the muscles (Kuster 1997).
A 2020 review: poles reduce the load on the legs but increase cardiovascular effort; with a heavy rucksack they can also help with balance.
The authors of the Alps study recommend regular physical activity with eccentric work (that of a muscle braking), but it is their opinion, not a finding.
encajar: Rest enough before starting the descent and take breaks on the way down: the authors of the Alps study recommend this.
Without trials of its own, the strength guidance is the general one, that of «Another sport».

lesiones.t: In hikers in the Austrian Alps (Alpine police data), about 75% of falls happened on the way down and almost 60% were due to slipping.

isla.t: Walking up to La Rambleta, on the Teide, requires a booking on Tenerife ON, and the trails may close because of ice, snow, wind or frost even if you have one.
On the Teide, altitude sickness usually brings a headache after 2–12 hours; with confusion, drowsiness, unsteady walking or breathlessness at rest, call 112 and go down with someone.
The sun is stronger at altitude: in August 2024, Izaña (2,371 m) recorded a UV index of 13.7, the highest AEMET registered that month. Protect yourself even if it feels cool.
In the heat, avoid walking in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
On the day of the hike, check Tenerife ON for alerts or closed trails; tell someone your route and do not go alone.

no: That strength training prevents falls or injuries in the mountains: we have not found any trial that tests this in hikers.
That poles always pay off: when walking without a load, the 2020 review advises weighing up the pros and cons.

deportes.t: The evidence points to maximal strength training out of the water being what most improves swimming performance, although 7 of 16 studies found no effect at all.
p: A review of 16 studies (Amaro et al. 2019): dry-land maximal strength training was the most effective method for performance; 7 studies found neither improvement nor worsening.
The same review puts forward plyometrics (jumps) as the most effective method for starts and turns.
deportes.dosis: The review mentions 6 to 12 weeks, with 2–4 sessions a week (about 24 in total), and its authors suggest 2–3 sets of 3–5 repetitions at 80–90% of the maximum you can lift once.
encajar: The review mentions programmes of 6 to 12 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect to swim better because of strength training: treat it as maintenance (deduction).
We have no data on combining strength training and swimming on the same day; in running and cycling, with 3 hours or more between the two there was no significant loss of explosive strength.

isla.t: Swim at beaches with lifeguards and always check the flag before going in. When the waves are unusually big, stay away from the sea; when there is a swell, do not do sport in the water.
If a current carries you away, do not swim against it: float so as not to tire yourself, wave your arm and shout for help, or swim out of it parallel to the shore.
According to the association Canarias, 1500 Km de Costa, of the 69 people who drowned in the Canary Islands in 2025, 74% were men and 46% had gone into the sea during a pre-alert or alert.
Swim parallel to the shore, with someone else and never at night; get out if you feel tired or cold, and do not drink alcohol if you are going to swim.
For sport in the heat, the WHO asks for sunscreen of factor 30 or more, a hat and sunglasses; the Government of the Canary Islands advises factor 50+, also on cloudy days.

no: That strength training makes you swim faster: almost half of the studies reviewed found no effect.
That jumps improve all your swimming: the review only puts them forward for starts and turns.

deportes.t: The evidence points to strength training with heavy loads slightly improving running economy, that is, using less energy at the same pace. Combining methods might help a little more, with low certainty.
p: A meta-analysis of 31 studies with 652 middle- and long-distance runners (Llanos-Lagos et al. 2024): heavy loads improved economy with a small effect and moderate certainty.
Combining methods, such as medium loads and jumps, had a moderate effect, but with low certainty; medium loads alone and isometrics (without movement) showed no effect.
Jumps (plyometrics) only improved economy at 12 km/h or less, that is, at 5:00 min/km or slower; in the main analysis they had no effect.
Heavy loads might pay off more in runners with a high VO2max (a lot of aerobic capacity) and at high speeds.
deportes.dosis: Heavy loads, of at least 80% of the maximum weight you can lift once, 2–4 days a week for 6–14 weeks; for example, half squats, leg presses and deadlifts.
encajar: In 43 studies, combining strength training with running or cycling did not reduce maximal strength or muscle; explosive strength did suffer, especially in the same session (Schumann 2022).
If you do both on the same day, leave at least 3 hours between running and strength training: with that gap there was no significant loss of explosive strength.
The programmes lasted 6 to 24 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect to run better because of strength training: treat it as maintenance (deduction).

isla.t: In the heat, avoid running in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
Acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks of sessions in the heat (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, run for less time, more gently and in the cooler hours.
The sun is stronger at altitude: in August 2024, Izaña (2,371 m) recorded a UV index of 13.7, the highest AEMET registered that month. Protect yourself even if it feels cool.
A one-day trip up the Teide does not acclimatise you to altitude: partial acclimatisation takes 5 to 7 days, according to the IOC consensus for athletes.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That it lowers your times: the meta-analysis measured running economy, which is not the same as your finishing time.
That any strength training will do: medium loads and isometrics did not improve running economy.
That there are as many data on women: only 180 of the 652 runners studied were women.

deportes.t: With low certainty, studies suggest that heavy leg strength training might improve pedalling efficiency, maximal power and performance, without changing maximal aerobic capacity (VO2max).
p: A meta-analysis of 17 studies with 262 cyclists (Llanos-Lagos et al. 2026): heavy strength training improved efficiency, peak power and performance; VO2max did not change.
Only two studies recruited women only; in total, 60 of the 262 participants were women.
deportes.dosis: Improvements likely from about 8 weeks or with 2 sessions a week, with heavy loads and 3–4 sets per exercise, in 4 leg exercises.
encajar: In season, 1 weekly session maintained the gains for 13 weeks in a study with cyclists; for health, the WHO asks adults for at least 2 days.
If you do strength training and cycling on the same day, leave at least 3 hours between them: with 20 minutes or less, explosive strength suffered (Schumann 2022).
Improvements seem likely from about 8 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect to pedal better because of strength training: treat it as maintenance (deduction).

isla.t: In the heat, avoid cycling in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
Acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks of sessions in the heat (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, shorter, easier rides in the cooler hours.
Climbing the Teide, the sun is stronger: in August 2024, Izaña (2,371 m) recorded a UV index of 13.7, the highest AEMET registered that month.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That strength training increases your aerobic capacity: VO2max did not change in these studies.
That the result is certain: the authors themselves rate the evidence as low certainty.

deportes.t: There are few studies: in one, maximal strength training with pull-ups and dips made surfers paddle faster, but no study has shown that it improves surfing on the wave.
p: A trial with competitive and recreational surfers (Coyne 2017): after training pull-ups and dips, they paddled faster in sprints of 5 to 15 m and over 400 m.
The improvement seemed to depend on starting strength and was greater in the weaker surfers (Coyne’s thesis, 2015).
A review of 8 studies (Donaldson 2022): maximal upper-body strength improved paddling, and training on unstable surfaces did not help.
deportes.dosis: Maximal-strength pull-ups and dips, 3 times a week for 5 weeks; the abstract and the thesis do not give the loads.
encajar: The trial lasted 5 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect to paddle faster because of strength training: treat it as maintenance (deduction).
In SUP, paddling more than 4.8 hours a week was a risk factor for injury, as were competing or being over 46 (Furness 2017).

lesiones.t: In 240 stand-up paddleboarders, more than half of them competitive, there were 3.63 injuries per 1,000 hours of practice (Furness 2017); we have no verified data for surfing.

isla.t: In the Canary Islands, beaches in the north are usually more dangerous than those in the south, because of the wind, the waves and the currents.
Before you go out, check the forecast: wind and sea can change suddenly on the coast. Do not go out at dusk or when there is a swell, and never alone.
If a current carries you away, do not paddle against it: stay with the board, which keeps you afloat (RNLI), call for help by waving your arm and get out parallel to the shore.
Use sun protection of factor 50+ and keep using it on cloudy days too, as the Government of the Canary Islands asks.

no: That strength training improves your surfing on the wave: no study in the review showed it.
That training on unstable surfaces will help you: in the review, it did not work.
That it applies equally to SUP: the trial was done with surfers, and for SUP we only have injury data.

deportes.t: We know of no strength studies in diving, but the Divers Alert Network (DAN) calls for sufficient strength, cardiovascular health and, above all, aerobic capacity for what the environment demands.
p: According to DAN, recreational diving can demand a moderate to high aerobic level, and freediving is considered vigorous exercise.
DAN considers regular physical activity, both aerobic and strength, essential, such as swimming lengths, strength training and flexibility and balance exercises.
encajar: At least 6 weeks before a diving trip, gradually increase your physical activity, as DAN advises.
If you are over 40 and do not exercise regularly, DAN advises seeing a doctor before you start training.
Do not dive if you are ill (DAN).

isla.t: Before flying, DAN asks for at least 12 hours after a no-decompression dive, 18 after several dives in a day or over several days, and substantially longer if you made decompression stops.
After diving, going up the Teide by car or cable car (up to 3,555 m) carries the same risk as flying and calls for the same waiting times, according to DAN Europe, from about 700 m of ascent.
Do not dive alone and mark where you are with a buoy, as the Government of the Canary Islands asks.
Before you go out, check the forecast: wind and sea can change suddenly on the coast. Do not go out at dusk.

no: That strength training makes you a better diver: we know of no studies that measure it; DAN includes it in general fitness.
That the waiting times before flying completely prevent decompression sickness: DAN says they do not guarantee it, and waiting longer reduces the risk.
That the waiting times apply if you have symptoms: DAN gives them for divers without symptoms; if you have any, get medical care.

deportes.t: A meta-analysis of 20 studies links greater jump power and greater upper-body explosive strength with greater clubhead speed; it is an association: training them might help, but we have no trials that prove it.
p: Brennan 2024: clubhead speed was associated with jump impulse (correlation zr 0.82), upper-body explosive strength (0.67) and jump power (0.66).
By contrast, flexibility and balance were not associated with clubhead speed (−0.04 and −0.06).
encajar: Without verified golf trials, the basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).

isla.t: In the heat, avoid playing in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
For sport in the heat, the WHO asks for sunscreen of factor 30 or more, a hat, sunglasses and loose, light-coloured clothing; the Government of the Canary Islands advises factor 50+.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That stretching or balance training gives you more clubhead speed: they were not associated with it.
More clubhead speed from strength training: what we have are associations, not trials.

deportes.t: We know of no strength studies in padel. In tennis, strength training and combined programmes increased serve speed, and isolated abs and lower back work did not (Deng 2025); in padel this can only be extrapolated to smashes (a deduction).
p: A meta-analysis of 16 studies with tennis players (Deng et al. 2025): strength training had a small effect on serve speed and combined programmes a moderate one.
In the combined programmes there was publication bias (studies with no effect may be missing): the authors call for more high-quality studies.
The meta-analysis only measured serve speed, in tennis players aged about 11 to 42, and does not mention padel.
deportes.dosis: In tennis players, strength training 2–3 times a week for 4–36 weeks; combined programmes, 3 times a week for 6–8 weeks (8–36 sessions).
encajar: The tennis programmes lasted 4 to 36 weeks, so in 1–2 weeks of holiday do not expect changes in your shots: treat it as maintenance (deduction).
The basis is the general one: in adults, strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups (ACSM 2026).

lesiones.t: In 8 studies, most of them in Spain, with 2,022 players: 3 injuries per 1,000 hours of training and 8 per 1,000 matches, mainly of tendons and muscles (Dahmen 2023).
zonas: Elbow: the most frequent, especially tennis elbow

isla.t: In the heat, avoid playing in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
If you arrive from a cooler climate, acclimatising to heat takes 1 to 2 weeks (Racinais 2015): for the first few days, shorter, easier matches.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.

no: That isolated abs and lower back work improves your shots: in tennis it did not increase serve speed.
That what applies to tennis applies to your serve: in padel the ball is struck at waist height or below.
Exact injury figures: the studies were of low to moderate quality and the literature is limited.

deportes.t: For a sport without its own guide, the basis is the general one: the WHO recommends that adults do strength training on at least 2 days a week with all the major muscle groups; from 5 to 17 years, at least 3.
p: WHO 2020: adults, 150–300 minutes a week of moderate activity or 75–150 of vigorous activity; from 5 to 17 years, an average of 60 minutes a day, moderate to vigorous.
According to the WHO, for all ages some physical activity is better than none.
From the age of 65, the WHO adds varied activity that emphasises balance and strength, on 3 or more days a week.
ACSM 2026, in healthy adults: training to muscular failure, choosing machines or free weights and complex periodisation (systematic variation) did not change results consistently.
deportes.dosis: For strength, the ACSM 2026 proposes loads of 80% of the maximum you can lift once and 2–3 sets per exercise; to build muscle, about 10 sets per muscle group per week.
encajar: Train all the major muscle groups on at least 2 days a week and build up gradually: it matters more than looking for a «perfect» plan (ACSM 2026, in adults).
If you combine strength training with running or cycling on the same day, leave at least 3 hours between them: with 20 minutes or less, explosive strength suffered (Schumann 2022).

isla.t: In the heat, avoid exercising in the middle of the day and drink water often, even if you are not thirsty.
The sun is stronger at altitude: in August 2024, Izaña (2,371 m) recorded a UV index of 13.7, the highest AEMET registered that month.
During calima, the Canary Islands health authorities ask people not to exercise outdoors, especially children, older people and people with respiratory or heart conditions.
If your sport is in the sea, swim at beaches with lifeguards and always check the flag before going in.

no: That general strength training improves your particular sport: without studies of that sport, we cannot say so.
That training to failure or a complex plan gives more results: the ACSM saw no consistent differences in healthy adults.
